answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through completed, escrowed jobs: a buyer funds a task, the agent delivers, and payment is released after a verifiable result, while disputes slash the agent’s bond. New identities start with no history, so splitting one operator across a hundred names does not multiply trust; each must earn it separately. A fake orchard delivery logged at the wharf earns nothing unless checked against the agreed proof at the vertex. The attacker must therefore lock real capital and repeat costly work, risking losses for every failed identity.
